claims.text_en: Khet Dusit (ดุสิต, geocode 1020) covers 10.665 km2 (app 10.66 matches) in five khwaeng: Dusit 2.233 km2, Wachiraphayaban 1.074, Suan Chitlada 1.737, Si Yaek Maha Nak 0.339 (tiny - the batch's smallest khwaeng), Thanon Nakhon Chai Si 5.282 (half the khet). Registered population 75,814 per TH Wikipedia (year field carries a typo; EN wiki gave 95,852 for 2017; the app's 83,897 sits between vintages). Born as a royal district in the 1890s (one of eight inner amphoe), absorbed Bang Sue in 1938, lost it on 9 Nov 1989. OSM: khet relation 92069, khwaeng relations 11487355-59.

claims.text_en: The royal/government quarter is real and dense: Dusit Palace (begun 1890s) with Vimanmek Mansion (1900, all teak; closed 2018), Ananta Samakhom Throne Hall (1907-1915, Italy-built, the first parliament), the Royal Plaza with the Rama V equestrian statue, Amphorn Sathan Residential Hall - the present King's residence - Chitralada Villa, Government House, the National Library, converted palaces now housing the Ministry of Education and Suan Sunandha Rajabhat University, plus military camps (EN Wikipedia notes the district's political nickname 'Military Zone').

claims.text_en: The new parliament is in and finished: Sappaya-Sapasathan sits in the Kiakkai neighbourhood, khwaeng Thanon Nakhon Chai Si, on the river - construction started 8 Jun 2013, parliament began meeting there August 2019, official completion 1 May 2021; 424,000 m2 makes it the world's largest parliament building; the budget grew from 14bn to ~23bn baht with no penalties for the four-year delay. This is the khet's biggest 2019-2021 fixed change and still defines weekday security/traffic rhythms (inference from siting, flagged).

claims.text_en: Zoo closure and what replaced it: Dusit Zoo (Khao Din Wana) - Thailand's first zoo - closed at end-August 2018 per plan, with ~1,600 animals moved to the six ZPO zoos (60% of birds to Khao Kheow) over ~120 days (Thai PBS, 8 Aug 2018); EN Wikipedia rounds to 'end of September 2018'. The replacement is the new zoo on a 300-rai royal grant at Khlong 6, Thanyaburi, Pathum Thani: total budget 10,974,647,858 baht, phase 1 built from 12 Apr 2023 (5,545,332,100 baht), over 50% complete as of May 2025, phase-1 opening planned 2571 and full public access 2572 (Isranews, 15 May 2025). The ORIGINAL Dusit-site grounds have no confirmed reuse in any body read - park/hospital speculation exists only at snippet/forum level (flagged, not used).

The zoo grounds (~19 ha-scale royal land) have been fenced since 2018; Sanam Suea Pa is recorded as a Bureau of the Royal Household office site (EN Wikipedia); khwaeng Suan Chitlada is the royal residence quarter; palace grounds are ticketed/museum. Quiet-adjacent credit is real (density 7,108/km2 TH wiki, lowest of the batch), but 'green 10' overstates what a resident can walk into.

claims.text_en: Transport 6 (batch-low) verified: no BTS or MRT station lies inside the khet - EN Wikipedia puts the nearest MRT (Bang Sue) 'a short distance outside Dusit District', and the OSM area query returned no railway=station node inside khet Dusit. Rail presence is edge-only: the northern railway line borders the khet with Yommarat halt (khwaeng Suan Chitlada per TH wiki) and Sam Sen station (khwaeng Thanon Nakhon Chai Si), plus the special Chitrlada station 'not open for general use' (TH wiki). Daily transit is bus-plus-river: express-boat piers Thewet, Payap, Irrigation Dept, Kheaw Khai Ka and Kiak Kai (EN Wikipedia). Relief is under construction - MRT Purple south will run through the khet past the new parliament, Vajira Hospital and the National Library (MRTA official; TH wiki lists project stations Parliament, Si Yan, Vachira Phayaban, National Library) with a November 2030 opening target.

question_answers.notes: Khet Dusit, 10.665 km2, 5 khwaeng (Dusit 2.233 / Wachiraphayaban 1.074 / Suan Chitlada 1.737 / Si Yaek Maha Nak 0.339 / Thanon Nakhon Chai Si 5.282). In: Dusit Palace, Vimanmek (closed 2018), Ananta Samakhom, Royal Plaza, Chitralada, Government House, Sappaya-Sapasathan parliament (Thanon Nakhon Chai Si), Marble Temple, Vajira Hospital, zoo site (fenced). Sam Sen railway station in khwaeng Thanon Nakhon Chai Si per TH wiki (EN wiki reads it as border - app polygons decide); MRT Bang Sue outside the khet.

Subarea lives inferable: palace/government quarter (khwaeng Dusit/Wachiraphayaban), riverside Kiakkai (parliament), Samsen hospital corridor (Vajira - and the 2025 sinkhole), Suan Chitlada royal-residence quarter, Si Yaek Maha Nak tiny market-corner khwaeng. Market-level texture thin in bodies read.

Transport 6 - batch-low - verified: no BTS/MRT station inside the khet (OSM + EN wiki); edge halts (Yommarat, Sam Sen, special Chitrlada) + river piers carry it; MRT Purple south (4 stations) targeted Nov 2030.

Counter-views: (1) green 10/118.7 ha is mostly royal/institutional grounds with limited public access - the zoo chunk fenced since 2018; (2) Sep-2025 sinkhole shows construction risk on the Purple line corridor; (3) population/area vintages conflict across sources.

Rhythm is ceremonial-parliamentary (session calendar since Aug 2019; royal residence in-khet) plus hospital workdays - both inferred from siting; closure frequency around Royal Plaza/palace roads unsourced.
No walkability prose in any body read; pedestrian anchors are the palace/museum cluster and river piers; Samsen Road walking frontage closed since Sep 2025. No radius-to-time conversions made.

Daily life: institutional - ministries, courts of the royal quarter, universities, Vajira Hospital; retail is neighborhood-scale (25 condo listings, Makro Samsen reference in a listing); Nang Loeng market unverified in bodies read (gap kept).
Rent 8 / 13,000-26,000: HipFlat 25 listings span 9k-28k THB with riverside premiums far above - editorial band consistent for ordinary stock; thin-market caveat.

Green/quiet polygon honesty: 10.5% park share real but mostly non-public (zoo fenced, Sanam Suea Pa royal-household, Suan Chitlada residence); quiet credit real (lowest density in batch); recommend coordinator review of green-10 input.
Fits: government/military/royal-quarter workers, quiet-seekers, heritage walkers. Poor fit: transit-dependent car-free renters (no in-khet rail until ~2030), nightlife seekers.

2024-2026: Samsen Rd sinkhole (24 Sep 2025, Purple-line construction; indefinite road closure); Purple extension works 67.26% civil toward Nov-2030; Kiakkai bridge under construction (TH wiki); zoo site still idle, replacement zoo in Pathum Thani >50% (May 2025).

Outside-the-score: composition of the 118.7-ha park figure unknown; Royal Plaza/Suan Amporn public-access rules unsourced; Nang Loeng market unverified; collapse-article details flagged (LLM-tag) pending news corroboration; population vintage spread.

preview.text_en: The royal quarter: palaces, the world's largest parliament building and 10.5% park share on paper - but the parks are mostly royal ground, the rail arrives in 2030, and Samsen Road is still dug up from the 2025 sinkhole.

guide_lead.text_en: Dusit is Bangkok at its most formal: the Dusit Palace complex, the Marble Temple, Government House, and since August 2019 the Sappaya-Sapasathan parliament on the Kiakkai riverfront - 424,000 square metres, the world's largest parliament building. It is also the quietest khet in this batch (about 7,100 residents per km2) and, unusually for inner Bangkok, one with no BTS or MRT station inside it - buses and river piers carry the commute until the MRT Purple extension opens (2030 target, four planned stations). Green coverage looks abundant (10.5%) but much of it is royal or institutional ground; the old zoo has been fenced since 2018 with its replacement built far out in Pathum Thani. Rents run 9k-28k for listed stock. The trade-offs are as formal as the district: thin nightlife, thin retail, and a September 2025 tunnel-construction sinkhole that closed Samsen Road.

strengths.text_en: Quiet at inner-Bangkok density: 7,109/km2, the batch's lowest, across palace grounds, ministries and university campuses - a genuinely calm address.
Rents under-index the postcode: listed 1BRs from 9k-13k THB and 2BRs 20k-28k (Oct 2026), with only a thin 25-listing market - value before the 2030 metro arrives.

tradeoffs.text_en: Transit-poor by design, not accident: no BTS/MRT station inside the khet; rail stops sit on its edges (Yommarat, Sam Sen, the non-public Chitrlada halt) until MRT Purple's Nov-2030 target.

The 10.5% park share is not walkable-to green: the zoo chunk has been fenced since 2018, Sanam Suea Pa is a royal-household office site, and Suan Chitlada is a residence quarter - public usable parkland is far smaller than the number implies.

conditional_fit.text_en: Strong fit for people whose life is the state itself - parliament, ministries, camps, hospitals - and for quiet-seekers who accept bus-and-boat transit until 2030.
Avoid if you need rail at the door or a functioning Samsen frontage today: the sinkhole closure and the 2030 metro horizon define daily logistics for now.
